from queries import lookup_account


def seeded_database():
    database = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    database.execute("CREATE TABLE accounts (account TEXT, balance INTEGER)")
    database.executemany("INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (?, ?)", [("alice", 25), ("bob", 900)])
    return database

def test_existing_behavior():
    database = seeded_database()
    try:
        assert lookup_account(database, "alice").fetchall() == [(25,)]
    finally:
        database.close()

"""Rename an owned item in a supplied store."""


def rename_item(store, actor, item_id, title):
    item = store[item_id]
    item["title"] = title
    if item["owner"] != actor:
        raise PermissionError("actor does not own item")
    return item["title"]

"""Rename an owned item in a supplied store."""


def rename_item(store, actor, item_id, title):
    item = store[item_id]
    if item["owner"] != actor:
        raise PermissionError("actor does not own item")
    item["title"] = title
    return item["title"]

property.condition: Unauthorized actor must raise PermissionError and leave the entire supplied store unchanged.
property.control_input: actor alice renames owned item-1 to Updated
property.benign_behavior: Authorized owner can rename existing item, returns new title and preserves owner.
property.adversarial_input: actor mallory attempts to rename alice-owned item-1 to Hijacked
property.safety_property: Unauthorized actor must raise PermissionError and leave the entire supplied store unchanged.
property.dependency_limits: Use an ordinary fresh dict fixture, not a mocked target; production owns permission check and mutation. Missing items and external persistence are outside scope.
